facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of watery diarrhea.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day history of watery diarrhea

facts.content: Diarrhea occurs every 10 minutes with urges recurring immediately after bowel movements.
facts.source_text: Diarrhea q10 min; urges recur immediately after BM; no hematochezia

facts.content: Patient has tender, central/infra-umbilical abdominal pain that is mild and eased after defecation.
facts.source_text: Central/infra-umbilical abd pain; mild; eased post-defecation; tender on self-palpation

facts.content: Patient had one episode of emesis this morning after eating fruit, with no blood in vomit.
facts.source_text: 1 episode emesis this morning after fruit; no hematemesis; nausea present

facts.content: Patient reports decreased oral intake and possible mild dehydration but is unsure about fever.
facts.source_text: ↓ oral intake; likely hypo-hydration; unsure fever (mild sweats x4 d)

facts.content: No chest pain is reported, and baseline asthma symptoms are present with no walking or talking difficulties.
facts.source_text: No chest pain; baseline asthma symptoms only; walking/talking OK

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
facts.source_text: PMH: Asthma

facts.content: Patient uses an inhaler with a brand that is unspecified and was recently switched.
facts.source_text: Meds: Inhaler (brand unspecified; recently switched)

facts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
facts.source_text: Allergies: NKDA

facts.content: Patient's father had bowel cancer and died 10 years ago.
facts.source_text: FH: Father – bowel CA (died 10 y ago)

facts.content: Acute gastroenteritis or food-borne illness is suspected due to watery diarrhea, mild abdominal pain, single emesis, and no blood in stools.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute gastroenteritis/food-borne illness – watery diarrhea, mild abd pain, single emesis, no blood

facts.content: There is a risk of mild dehydration due to ongoing fluid losses and decreased intake.
facts.source_text: 2. Risk of mild dehydration – ongoing fluid losses, ↓ intake

facts.content: Asthma is stable with continued use of the usual inhaler.
facts.source_text: 3. Asthma – stable, usual inhaler use

facts.content: Family history of colorectal cancer causes patient anxiety, but there are no current red-flag features.
facts.source_text: 4. Family history colorectal cancer – pt anxiety, no current red-flag features

facts.content: Increase oral fluids or use oral rehydration solutions with small, frequent sips.
facts.source_text: ↑ Oral fluids / ORS; small frequent sips

facts.content: Follow a BRAT or bland diet as tolerated and rest at home.
facts.source_text: BRAT/bland diet as tolerated; rest at home

facts.content: Do not use antibiotics as they may worsen the illness.
facts.source_text: No antibiotics; may worsen course

facts.content: Seek medical help if fever, blood in stool, blood in vomit, persistent vomiting, escalating pain, signs of dehydration, or symptoms persist for more than 3–4 days.
facts.source_text: Red-flags: seek GP/ED if fever, hematochezia/melena, hematemesis, persistent vomiting, escalating pain, signs of dehydration, >3–4 d symptoms

facts.content: Continue using inhaler as needed for asthma symptoms.
facts.source_text: Continue inhaler; use PRN for asthma

facts.content: Follow up with GP if there is no improvement in 1-2 days or to discuss CRC screening due to family history.
facts.source_text: GP f/u if no improvement in 1–2 d or for CRC screening discussion given FH
